turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to start biking to work instead of taking the bus.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Love that. There's the quick route along the main road or the longer one through the park. Which sounds better to you?

contexts.pending: main road route or park route to work
think_reask: So, have you picked a route? The quicker main road or the longer park path?
Okay, time's up. Main road or through the park for your commute?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were choosing your bike route to work, main road or park.
Hi again. Did you settle on a commute route, the fast road or the park?

endings.user: The park, I'd rather not ride next to all those trucks.
endings.moshi: Good call. Leave about ten minutes earlier and you'll be fine.

endings.user: Main road, I really can't spare the extra time in the morning.
endings.moshi: Okay. Wear something bright and use a front light, even in daylight.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My bike's back tire has gone flat again.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Annoying. You could patch the inner tube yourself tonight, or take it to the shop tomorrow and get a sturdier tire. What would you like to do?

contexts.pending: patch the tube or take it to the shop
think_reask: So what's the plan for that flat tire? Patch it yourself or go to the shop?
Have you decided? Fix the tube tonight or let the shop handle it?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were sorting out your flat tire, patching it or taking it in.
There you are. Still deciding between patching the tube and visiting the bike shop?

endings.user: I'll patch it, I've got a kit somewhere in the garage.
endings.moshi: Great. Check the inside of the tire for a thorn first, or it'll go flat again.

endings.user: Shop, I think. If it keeps happening I want a better tire.
endings.moshi: That makes sense. Ask them about a puncture resistant tire.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A few friends invited me on a long weekend ride.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fun! They're doing either the flat forty mile loop or the hilly twenty five mile one. Which do you think your legs can handle?

contexts.pending: flat long loop or short hilly ride
think_reask: Okay, so which ride are you joining? The flat long loop or the short hilly one?
Have you made up your mind? Forty flat miles or twenty five with hills?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were picking the weekend ride, flat and long or short and hilly.
Hi again. Did you decide which group ride to do?

endings.user: The flat one. Hills and I are not friends.
endings.moshi: Fair. Bring two water bottles and a snack for the halfway point.

endings.user: Let's do the hilly one, I could use the challenge.
endings.moshi: Nice. Shift into an easy gear early before each climb.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, can I borrow your helmet tomorrow? Mine's cracked.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Sure, but it might be a little big for you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It has that little dial in the back, right?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Yeah, just tighten it. It's on the hook by the door.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Thanks, I'll order a new one tonight.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Did you lock the bikes up outside?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I locked mine. I thought you did yours.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, I came in through the back. Is it just leaning against the fence?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I think so. Want me to go check?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Would you? The key is on the little table.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Got it. Back in a minute.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So how was the ride along the river this morning?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Beautiful, but so windy on the way back.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How far did you go?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: All the way to the old bridge and back. My legs are dead.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Next time wake me up, I want to come.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I tried! You told me to go away.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, fair. Set an alarm for both of us then.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How often should I pump up my bike tires?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For a road bike, about once a week. Thinner tires lose air faster than you'd think.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And how do I know the right pressure?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's printed on the side of the tire as a range. Aim somewhere in the middle for everyday riding.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've just been squeezing them / and guessing, honestly.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A lot of people do. A floor pump with a gauge takes the guessing out and isn't expensive.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I go lower if it's raining?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A little lower, yes. It gives you more grip on wet roads.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My chain makes this squeaking noise every time I pedal.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That usually means it's dry. A bit of chain lube should fix it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I just use cooking oil?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: I wouldn't. It gets sticky and collects dirt. Proper bike lube is cheap and lasts a long time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. How do I put it on?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Put one drop on each link while you slowly turn the pedals backward. Then wipe off the extra with a rag.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I clean it first, or / is that overkill?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If it looks black and gritty, wipe it down first. Otherwise you're just mixing new oil with old dirt.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is it a bad idea to bike in the winter?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not at all, lots of people do. You just need good lights, warm gloves and a bit more caution on ice.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about my hands? They freeze even in fall.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try lobster style gloves, they keep fingers together for warmth but still let you brake easily.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm, actually maybe I'll just / take the bus when it snows.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a sensible compromise. Ride on dry days and skip the icy ones.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do I need special tires for the cold days?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not for dry cold. Studded tires only really matter if you plan to ride on ice.

option_sets.lead_in: I need a new bike and I've narrowed it down, but I'm stuck.
options: The first one is a light road bike, really fast, but it has thin tires and no rack.
Then there's a hybrid with wider tires, a rack on the back and a more upright seat.
And the last one is an electric bike, heavy and pricey, but hills would be no problem at all.
moshi_comment: It depends on what you'll use it for. The road bike is great for fitness rides but awkward for carrying groceries, while the hybrid handles commuting and errands easily. The electric bike makes sense if your route is hilly and you don't want to arrive sweaty.
The hybrid sounds like the best all rounder of the three. How long and how hilly is your usual ride? If it's steep, the electric bike might be worth the price.

option_sets.lead_in: We're planning a cycling day trip and I can't decide on the route.
options: One route follows the coast, about thirty miles, flat, with a nice cafe at the end.
Another one goes up through the vineyards, shorter, but with two pretty steep climbs.
The third is a forest trail, mostly gravel, quiet and shady, maybe twenty miles.
moshi_comment: The coast route is the easiest and the cafe makes a great finish. The vineyard route has the best views, but those climbs could wear out a mixed group. The forest trail is lovely on a hot day, as long as everyone's bike can handle gravel.
I'd pick the coast unless your group loves hills. Are all of you on road bikes? If so, I'd skip the gravel forest trail.
